title: Cop assault concocted, lawyer says: Officer already on trial facing more accusations of using excessive force
article: A carpenter who alleges police brutality denies he levelled the accusation only after learning the Toronto officer was already facing an allegation of excessive force.
"That was why he was a target," said defence lawyer Peter Brauti, not specifying what the other allegation was about.

"Not at all," responded Shayne Fisher. The 29-year-old man was acquitted in 2008 of firearms charges after a judge ruled he and a co-accused had been physically abused by police during a raid on a Lawrence Ave. W. apartment on June 7, 2006.

The Special Investigations Unit charged Det.-Const. Gerrard Arulanandam in 2010 after reading about the case in the Star. The SIU is the province's civilian agency that investigates cases of serious injury or death involving police.
Arulanandam has pleaded not guilty to assault causing bodily harm and uttering threats. Justice Harriet Sachs is hearing the case without a jury.
Fisher suffered a fractured rib, perforated eardrum and badly swollen eye when he was arrested in a neighbour's apartment. He has no criminal record.
Fisher's trial lawyer, Allan Lobel, told the Star it is preposterous to suggest his client accused Arulanandam of assaulting him only after learning of the officer's history.
It was during the trial that the defence discovered Arulanandam had previously been investigated and cleared by the SIU in the fatal shooting of a suspected drug dealer in 2004.
Arulanandam was also cleared of a complaint that he held a gun to a suspect's head in 2005.
"We had no inkling about any of that," Lobel said Tuesday.
Court transcripts show Arulanandam shot Courtney Peters.

An SIU news release announcing that an officer was legally justified in fatally shooting Peters did not identify Arulanandam. The SIU doesn't typically release the name of "subject officers" unless they've been charged, a spokeswoman said in an email.

The news release said "the officer had a reasonable and honestly held belief that Mr. Peters posed a real and imminent threat to the officer's life and safety and to the lives and safety of those in the vicinity."
